items.title: EcoNav AI: An AI-Powered Disaster Assistance System with Offline Chatbot and Navigation
items.abstract: Natural disasters frequently damage mobile towers and power supply, leaving affected people without internet access ex-actly when they need maps, first-aid instructions and a way to call for help. Most disaster-management applications depend on cloud services and centralized networks, so they fail under these conditions. This paper presents EcoNav AI, an offline-first mobile disaster assistance system that integrates (i) an on-device AI chat-bot for emergency and first-aid guidance, (ii) GPS-based navigation over pre-downloaded OpenStreetMap data, (iii) locally stored infor-mation on shelters, hospitals, food and water points, (iv) a one-tap SOS alert carrying the available GPS location, and (v) peer-to-peer messaging over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) and Wi-Fi Direct. All data are held in a local SQLite database so that core functions work without a network. We survey twenty recent studies on dis-aster communication, AI-based decision support and situational awareness, identify the lack of an integrated, resource-efficient offline platform, and propose a modular architecture together with Level 0 and Level 1 data-flow models, a local data schema and hardware/software requirements. This work reports the design stage (Phase I); implementation and field evaluation are planned as future work

items.title: Effect of Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Instruction on Students' Achievement and Interest in Basic Science and Technology in Secondary Schools in Imo State
items.abstract: This study investigated the effect of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted instruction on students’ achievement and interest in Basic Science and Technology in secondary schools in Imo State, Nigeria. It also examined gender differences in achievement and interest among students exposed to AI- assisted instruction. The study adopted a quasi- experimental, non- randomized pretest- posttest control group design. The study involved 120 Junior Secondary School Two (JSS II) students drawn from four public secondary schools, with 60 students in the AI- assisted instruction group and 60 in the conventional teaching group. Data were collected using the Basic Science and Technology Achievement Test (BSTAT) and the Basic Science and Technology Interest Scale (BSTIS).

items.abstract: This study examined the effect of project management practices on the performance of the TVET empowerment project in Rwanda, with particular focus on TVET graduates participating in workplace learning at "T-Kay Ltd.Data were collected using documentary review and questionnaires.A correlational research design was employed to examine the relationships between the study variables.The findings revealed that project management practices were generally implemented effectively within the T-KAY Limited TVET Graduates Project.Scope management practices recorded strong performance and significantly influenced project performance (β = 0.193, p < 0.05).Monitoring and evaluation demonstrated a strong positive relationship with project performance (r = 0.775, p < 0.01) but exhibited a statistically insignificant independent effect in the regression model (p > 0.05).Risk management emerged as the strongest predictor of project performance (β = 0.546, p < 0.05), confirming the importance of effective risk identification, mitigation, monitoring and corrective interventions.Stakeholder engagement also demonstrated a strong positive association with project performance (r = 0.907, p < 0.01), although its independent contribution was statistically insignificant in the regression model.The study concludes that project management practices significantly influence the performance of TVET empowerment projects, with scope management and risk management emerging as key determinants of project success.The study recommends strengthening entrepreneurship support mechanisms, beneficiary-centered monitoring systems, proactive risk management approaches, and stakeholder collaboration in order to enhance project sustainability, employment creation, and fulfillment of beneficiaries' expectations.

items.title: Effectiveness of Drive-Fun Intervention: Randomized Controlled Trial to Reduce Driving Risks Among Adolescents With ADHD
items.abstract: Importance Adolescents with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) are more likely to be involved in motor vehicle accidents, highlighting the need for early intervention. However, there is a lack of evidence-based interventions addressing driving safety in this population. Objective To evaluate the effectiveness of the Drive-Fun cognitive-functional intervention on simulated driving performance, attentional control, and visual scanning in adolescents with ADHD. Design Randomized controlled trial with three parallel groups: Drive-Fun, an educational intervention, and a control group. Setting A university research laboratory. Participants Ninety-three adolescents ( M age = 16.8 years, SD = 0.52) diagnosed with ADHD. Outcomes and Measures Primary outcomes were simulated driving errors; secondary outcomes included the percentage of time spent within the optimal Cognitive Effort Index (CEI) range and eye-tracking metrics. Results The Drive-Fun group demonstrated significant time-by-group interactions: reduced driving errors, F (2, 89) = 82.65, p < .001; increased percentage of time spent within the optimal CEI range, F (2, 89) = 15.56, p < .001; fewer dashboard fixations, F (2, 89) = 27.65, p < .001; and more fixations on traffic lights, F (2, 89) = 7.61, p = .001, and pedestrians, F (2, 89) = 10.15, p < .001. Exploratory moderation analyses indicated greater improvements in driving performance among adolescents with lower Conners Hyperactive Scores and no regular sports participation within the Drive-Fun group. Conclusions and Relevance The Drive-Fun intervention improved simulated driving performance, cognitive engagement, and visual scanning, indicating its potential to reduce driving-related risks among adolescents with ADHD. Improvements were maintained at follow up, indicating sustained benefits. These findings support integrating cognitive-functional strategies and simulation-based training into occupational therapy to enhance adolescents’ driving readiness and safety.

items.title: Effectiveness of exercise therapy in managing low back pain among industrial workers: a protocol of a systematic literature review
items.abstract: Low back pain is among the most common and debilitating musculoskeletal disorders worldwide, with industrial workers particularly at risk due to high physical demands and biomechanical stressors in their work environments. Despite broad evidence supporting exercise therapy for managing low back pain in general populations, the effectiveness and applicability of structured exercise programs among industrial workers remain underexplored. This systematic review aims to evaluate the effectiveness of exercise-based interventions specifically targeting non-specific low back pain in industrial settings. This systematic review will encompass randomized controlled trials and controlled quasi-experimental studies that examine structured exercise interventions, such as strength training, core stabilization, or motor control therapy among adult industrial workers with non-specific low back pain of any symptom duration (acute < 6 weeks, subacute 6–12 weeks, or chronic > 12 weeks). Eligible studies must compare exercise interventions with usual care, non-exercise controls, or other types of exercise programs. Primary outcomes are pain intensity and functional disability, with short-term follow-up as the primary time point. Secondary outcomes are work participation (return-to-work and absenteeism), recurrence, quality of life, work ability and adverse events. The search strategy will involve a three-step process: initial exploratory search in PubMed, comprehensive database searching using identified keywords and index terms, and manual reference list screening. Databases to be searched include PubMed, CINAHL, CENTRAL (Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials), SCOPUS, and ProQuest for gray literature. Two independent reviewers will screen articles using Rayyan software, extract relevant data using a standardized form, and assess methodological quality using validated tools. Randomized and quasi-experimental studies will be synthesized separately, and a narrative synthesis will be performed in accordance with the Synthesis Without Meta-analysis (SWiM) reporting guideline. The review will provide a focused synthesis of the evidence regarding the effectiveness of structured exercise therapy in managing low back pain among industrial workers. It aims to summarize the existing evidence and may help identify implications for occupational health practice and priorities for future research, particularly regarding longer-term outcomes and implementation in high-demand labor environments. items.title: Effects of acupuncture-assisted power nap on presenteeism, fatigue, and psychomotor vigilance in female workers with self-reported fatigue: a randomized controlled trial
items.abstract: Background Fatigue and presenteeism are major contributors to productivity loss and have become important targets of occupational health and health and productivity management programs. Although power naps are known to reduce fatigue and improve alertness, whether acupuncture enhances these effects remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether acupuncture-assisted power naps could improve work performance outcomes beyond the effects of power naps alone in female workers with self-reported fatigue. Methods Sixty-one female workers with self-reported fatigue from seven companies and healthcare institutions in Japan were randomized to the power nap group ( n = 29) or the acupuncture-assisted power nap group ( n = 32). Two randomized participants did not receive the allocated intervention or provide post-baseline outcome data; consequently, 59 participants (28 and 31, respectively) were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis. Participants received a 20-min power nap twice weekly for 8 weeks, with the intervention group receiving acupuncture during the nap period. The primary outcomes were subjective fatigue, assessed using the Japan National Institute of Occupational Safety and Health Fatigue Checker, and psychomotor vigilance, measured using the Psychomotor Vigilance Test (PVT). The prespecified secondary outcome was presenteeism (absolute and relative presenteeism), assessed using the World Health Organization Health and Work Performance Questionnaire. Absolute and relative absenteeism were additionally analyzed as exploratory outcomes. Outcomes were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models. Results No significant group-by-time interactions were observed for fatigue ( F = 0.79, p = 0.457) or PVT reaction time ( F = 0.62, p = 0.543). In unadjusted analyses, significant group-by-time interactions were observed for absolute ( F = 7.92, p < 0.001) and relative presenteeism ( F = 3.65, p = 0.029). In adjusted sensitivity analyses, the interaction remained significant for absolute presenteeism ( F = 9.57, p = 0.003) but was no longer significant for relative presenteeism ( F = 2.11, p = 0.152). In exploratory analyses, no significant group-by-time interactions were observed for absenteeism. Conclusion No additional benefit of acupuncture-assisted power naps over power naps alone was demonstrated for short-term fatigue or psychomotor vigilance. Favorable findings for presenteeism were observed in secondary analyses, but these findings were attenuated after adjustment, particularly for relative presenteeism, and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory. items.title: El uso de la tecnología educativa en la enseñanza de la geología en Educación Secundaria Obligatoria y Enseñanza Universitaria
items.abstract: The use of educational technology has transformed teaching and learning methods, particularly in disciplines such as geology. The main aim of this study is to analyze the application of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), including Artificial Intelligence (AI), in the classroom and to assess its impact on academic performance and student motivation in the teaching and learning of geology in compulsory secondary education and higher education. The study consisted of a systematic literature review of 25 scientific publications using PRISMA 2020. The results indicate that educational technology complements conventional teaching methods through simulations, interactive resources, and virtual environments, and promotes understanding of abstract concepts and meaningful learning. However, several barriers to integration remain, including insufficient teacher training, resistance to methodological change, and limited infrastructure and access to technology.

Conventional viral vectors and synthetic nanocarriers are associated with challenges including immunogenicity, limited cargo capacity, prolonged nuclease expression, off-target effects, and manufacturing complexities. Engineered extracellular vesicles (EVs) are being investigated as alternative delivery carriers due to their biological origin, capacity for cargo encapsulation, and opportunities for surface functionalization. However, their biocompatibility, immunogenicity, and ability to cross biological barriers depend on vesicle source, formulation, and experimental conditions. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in the design of engineered EVs for CRISPR/Cas delivery, with a particular focus on strategies to improve cargo loading, targeting specificity, and therapeutic efficacy. We discuss the advantages and limitations of different CRISPR cargo formats, including plasmid DNA, mRNA, and ribonucleoprotein complexes, together with endogenous and exogenous loading approaches, hybrid EV platforms, and methods for enhancing intracellular delivery. Advances in EV surface engineering through genetic, chemical, physical, and biomimetic modifications are highlighted as strategies being investigated to improve tissue-specific delivery and functional cargo transport. The review also highlights emerging research directions, including CRISPR-EV theranostic platforms and the application of artificial intelligence to enhance CRISPR-EV therapeutic systems. Finally, key translational challenges, including scalable production, EV heterogeneity, cargo-loading efficiency, biodistribution, regulatory standardization, and quality control, are critically discussed. EV-mediated CRISPR delivery remains at an early preclinical stage, with clinical safety and therapeutic efficacy yet to be established. Further advances in EV engineering, cargo-loading strategies, and manufacturing standardization are needed to support its potential clinical translation.

items.title: Enhancing corporate sustainability performance through tacit knowledge management: the dual mediation of green business strategy and generative AI with top management support
items.abstract: Purpose Amid escalating global environmental and social pressures, corporate sustainability performance (CSP) has become a critical strategic imperative, particularly for highly polluting sectors. Drawing on the natural resource-based view and dynamic capabilities theory, this study aims to examine the impact of tacit knowledge management process (TKMP), particularly knowledge acquisition, sharing and application on the CSP of steel industry in China. Furthermore, it explores the dual mediating mechanisms of green business strategy (GBS) and generative artificial intelligence (GAI) in translating TKMP into CSP, while examining top management support (TMS) as a boundary condition moderating the relationship between the TKMP dimensions and GBS. Design/methodology/approach The study gathered data from 357 employees of steel manufacturing companies in China using survey questionnaires. The study used smart-PLS to examine both measurement and structural models. Findings The results showed that all three dimensions of TKMP are positively associated with CSP. GBS and GAI significantly mediate the relationships between the TKMP dimensions and CSP (complementary partial mediation). In addition, TMS positively moderates (strengthens) the relationship between tacit knowledge application and GBS, but it negatively moderates (weakens) the relationship between tacit knowledge acquisition and GBS and it does not significantly moderate the relationship for knowledge sharing. Originality/value These findings provide theoretical insights into how intangible knowledge resources and advanced artificial intelligence can jointly support sustainability, offering practical guidance for policymakers and managers seeking to leverage TKMP and GAI to achieve environmental and social objectives in heavy manufacturing contexts.

items.title: Enhancing Pedagogical Practices Through Generative AI: Recommendations for DepEd Policy Development
items.abstract: This study examined public-school teachers’ readiness, utilization, challenges, and ethical practices regarding generative artificial intelligence (Gen AI) in the Department of Education–National Capital Region (DepEd NCR), with the aim of developing policy recommendations for responsible and equitable classroom integration. Guided by the Technology Acceptance Model, the research employed an embedded mixed-methods design using questionnaire responses from 454 teachers across 16 school divisions and in-depth interviews with 18 educators during academic year 2024–2025. Quantitative responses were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative interview accounts were organized through thematic analysis to contextualize teachers’ experiences. The findings described moderate teacher readiness and uneven use of Gen AI, with applications more evident in lesson planning and instructional preparation than in assessment and student engagement. Participants identified insufficient training, unequal connectivity and device access, curriculum-alignment concerns, and uncertainty about ethical responsibilities as important constraints. Teachers also described efforts to verify AI-generated content, protect student information, and preserve instructional judgment. Based on the combined evidence, the study proposed a policy framework emphasizing differentiated professional development, infrastructure support, ethical safeguards, implementation monitoring, and sustained teacher participation. The November 2026 publication update situates these 2024–2025 findings within subsequently issued national guidance, without treating the update as new empirical data.
